department: University of the Philippines Diliman Department of Philosophy
location: 2/F Palma Hall Pavilion 2, Quirino Avenue, UP Diliman, Quezon City
status: Prototype // Subject to ongoing academic assessment and revision
disclaimer: This academic genealogy dataset is a research prototype. Information presented is preliminary, undergoing continuous archival verification, and subject to change.

student_organizations.name: UP Philosophical Society (UP PhiloSoc)
student_organizations.description: True to its 58 years of existence, UP PhiloSoc is not only a haven for liberal philosophical learning, but a breeding ground for effective, critical, and responsible leaders and thinkers of society in whatever field they may be a part of. Members pursue professions such as law, public governance, journalism, research, and education. Organizes philosophical discussions, lecture series, and philosophy tutorials.

student_organizations.name: UP Kabataang Pilosopo Tasyo (UP KAPITAS)
student_organizations.description: Isang sosyo-akademikong samahan para sa mga mag-aaral ng Kagawaran ng Pilosopiya sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas Diliman. Layunin nito na paunlarin ang pilosopiyang Pilipino na angkop at makabuluhan sa lipunang Pilipino; humubog ng mga Pilipinong palaisip na nais paglingkuran ang sambayanan; magbigay ng espasyo para sa mga gawaing pilosopikal; at isulong ang pilosopiya bilang isang disiplina.

student_organizations.name: Apeiron Core Group
student_organizations.description: Serves as the official student volunteer arm of the UP Diliman Department of Philosophy. Committed to addressing Department needs and concerns, delivering basic student services, and forwarding relevant university and national campaigns.

nodes.name: Henry S. Townsend
nodes.institution: University of Chicago / Des Moines College
nodes.tradition: Early Pragmatism, Logic, Educational Philosophy
nodes.dissertation: Educational and Philosophical Foundations in the Philippine Islands
nodes.bio: First Head of the joint Department of Philosophy and Psychology established in 1910 at the University of the Philippines Manila campus (Padre Faura); oversaw the initial curriculum of philosophical and psychological studies during the American occupation before the post-war transfer to Diliman.

nodes.name: Friedrich Ludwig Gottlob Frege
nodes.tradition: Mathematical Logic, Philosophy of Language
nodes.dissertation: Über eine geometrische Darstellung der imaginären Gebilde in der Ebene
nodes.bio: Foundational figure in modern mathematical logic and analytic philosophy; intellectual predecessor whose lectures and works shaped Rudolf Carnap at the University of Jena.

nodes.name: Rudolf Carnap
nodes.tradition: Logical Positivism, Semantics, Philosophy of Science
nodes.dissertation: Der Raum: Ein Beitrag zur Wissenschaftslehre
nodes.bio: Pivotal member of the Vienna Circle and major proponent of logical empiricism; professor at the University of Chicago where he supervised Ricardo R. Pascual's doctoral dissertation.

nodes.name: Charles W. Morris
nodes.tradition: Pragmatism, Semiotics, Logical Empiricism
nodes.dissertation: Symbolism and Reality
nodes.bio: American semiotician and pragmatist at the University of Chicago; co-advisor and collaborator on the International Encyclopedia of Unified Science alongside Carnap, mentoring Ricardo Pascual.

nodes.name: B. F. Skinner
nodes.tradition: Radical Behaviorism, Epistemology of Science
nodes.dissertation: The Concept of the Reflex in the Description of Behavior
nodes.bio: Renowned Harvard epistemologist of behavior and experimental psychologist; doctoral dissertation supervisor of Alfredo V. Lagmay at Harvard University.

nodes.name: William Tuthill Parry
nodes.tradition: Analytic Logic, Modal Logic, Epistemology
nodes.dissertation: Implication and the Principles of Deductive Systems
nodes.bio: American logician known for the theory of analytic implication; supervised Armando F. Bonifacio's doctoral dissertation at the State University of New York at Buffalo.

nodes.name: Donald Evans
nodes.tradition: Bioethics, Medical Jurisprudence, Moral Philosophy
nodes.dissertation: Ethics and Medical Practice
nodes.bio: Director of the Centre for Philosophy and Health Care at the University of Wales Swansea; primary doctoral supervisor of Leonardo D. de Castro.

nodes.name: Ricardo R. Pascual
nodes.tradition: Logical Positivism, Epistemology, Philippine Thought
nodes.dissertation: Logical Analysis
nodes.bio: Pioneer of Anglo-American analytic philosophy in the Philippines. First Filipino to earn a PhD in philosophy; spearheaded the establishment of an independent UP Department of Philosophy in Diliman after WWII; cultivated the celebrated 'Pasky Boys'.

nodes.name: Alfredo V. Lagmay
nodes.role: Former Instructor in Philosophy & Alumnus (Ph.B., M.A.)
nodes.tradition: Logic, Epistemology, Philosophy of Mind
nodes.dissertation: A Logical Analysis of the Concept of Mind and Conditioning
nodes.bio: Alumnus and former faculty member of the UP Department of Philosophy. Earned his Ph.B. (1947, cum laude) and M.A. in Philosophy (1951) under Dr. Ricardo R. Pascual. Served as an Instructor in Philosophy handling logic and philosophical analysis during the post-war Padre Faura and early Diliman periods before pursuing doctoral studies at Harvard. Did not become a professor of philosophy; his teaching and academic appointment in the department were as an instructor and alumnus.

nodes.name: Cesar Adib Majul
nodes.role: Assistant Head of Philosophy (1959) & Dean of Arts and Sciences
nodes.tradition: Islamic Philosophy, Political Thought, Historiography
nodes.dissertation: The Political and Constitutional Ideas of the Philippine Revolution
nodes.bio: Seminal Philippine political philosopher and historian; served as Assistant Head of the Department of Philosophy in 1959 under Ricardo Pascual. Later served as Dean of University College (1961–1966), Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences (1969–1971), and designated University Professor (1979). Not an emeritus of the department.

nodes.name: Armando F. Bonifacio
nodes.institution: State University of New York at Buffalo
nodes.tradition: Analytic Philosophy, Epistemology, Philosophy of Education
nodes.dissertation: The Concept of Obligation
nodes.bio: Foundational figure in modern analytic philosophy at UP Diliman; served as Department Chairperson for eighteen years (1968–1986); conferred Professor Emeritus in 1987; shaped generations of Filipino philosophers.

nodes.name: Leonardo D. de Castro
nodes.tradition: Bioethics, Applied Ethics, Ethical Theory
nodes.dissertation: The Concept of Rules
nodes.bio: Pioneer of Bioethics in Asia; Centennial Professor and long-time Chair of the UP Diliman Department of Philosophy; Editor-in-Chief of Asian Bioethics Review; Vice-Chair of the UNESCO International Bioethics Committee.

nodes.name: Zosimo E. Lee
nodes.institution: State University of New York at Buffalo
nodes.tradition: Social & Political Philosophy, Rawlsian Liberalism, P4C
nodes.dissertation: Autonomy, Rationality, and the Public Sphere in Political Liberalism
nodes.bio: Affectionately remembered as the 'Walking Dean'; Dean of the College of Social Sciences and Philosophy (2004–2010); introduced Philosophy for Children (P4C) to the Philippines; prominent Rawlsian scholar.

nodes.name: Earl Stanley B. Fronda
nodes.tradition: Philosophy of Religion, Wittgenstein, Analytic Epistemology
nodes.dissertation: Wittgenstein's Philosophy of Religion: Faith, Reason, and Form of Life
nodes.bio: Professor and former department chairperson; authority on Ludwig Wittgenstein, philosophy of religion, and analytic epistemology; prolific author of philosophical treatises.

nodes.name: Ciriaco M. Sayson, Jr.
nodes.tradition: Ancient Philosophy, Aristotle, Metaphysics, Logic
nodes.dissertation: Aristotle on Substance, Matter, and Form
nodes.bio: Former Department Chairperson; leading scholar in classical Greek metaphysics, Aristotle, and formal logic; convener of major international philosophy symposiums at UP Diliman.

nodes.name: Ma. Theresa T. Payongayong
nodes.tradition: Feminist Philosophy, Filipino Philosophy, Philosophy for Children
nodes.dissertation: Feministang Pilosopiya sa Kontekstong Pilipino: Kritika at Pagpapalawig
nodes.bio: Professor and former Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs at UP Diliman; leading voice in Filipino feminist philosophy, gender discourse, indigenous philosophy, and Philosophy for Children.

nodes.name: Ma. Liza Ruth A. Ocampo
nodes.tradition: Metaphysics, Philosophical Anthropology, Medieval Philosophy, Thomas Aquinas
nodes.dissertation: The Dignity of the Thinking Person: A Philosophical Reflection on Human Nature
nodes.bio: Professor and former Department Chairperson (2023); recipient of the UP Diliman Centennial Professorial Chair; author of 'Break Open a Stone: An Invitation to Metaphysics' and 'The Dignity of the Thinking Person'; leading authority on Thomistic metaphysics.

nodes.name: Jeanette L. Yasol-Naval
nodes.tradition: Environmental Philosophy and Ethics, Pilosopiyang Filipino, EcoFeminism
nodes.dissertation: Environmental Justice and Ecological Sustainability in Developing Economies
nodes.bio: Professor with extensive publications in environmental philosophy, ethics of food, agricultural ethics, Philosophy for Children, indigenous cultures, and ecofeminism.

nodes.name: John Ian Boongaling
nodes.tradition: Epistemology, Logic, Philosophy of Mind, Philosophy of Language
nodes.dissertation: Dissolving the Gettier Problem: Beyond Analysis
nodes.bio: Full Professor specializing in epistemology, analytic logic, and philosophy of mind; author of 'Dissolving the Gettier Problem: Beyond Analysis' (Cambridge Scholars Publishing, 2020); prolific writer on Hintikka's epistemology, Aristotle's logic, and semantic theories.

nodes.name: Karen Connie Abalos-Orendain
nodes.tradition: Socio-Political Philosophy, Contemporary Philosophy, Japanese Philosophy, Immigration
nodes.dissertation: Cosmopolitan Norms, Democratic Legitimacy, and the Rights of Migrant Workers
nodes.bio: Professor and former Department Chairperson (2021–2023); Monbukagakusho scholar at Kobe University; recipient of ONE UP Professorial Chair Award in Applied Ethics; researcher on cosmopolitanism, deliberative democracy, and Japanese philosophy.

nodes.name: Lily Beth C. Lumagbas
nodes.tradition: Ancient Philosophy, Moral Philosophy, Platonic Ethics
nodes.dissertation: Virtue, Eudaimonia, and Moral Motivation in Platonic Dialogues
nodes.bio: Current Chairperson of the UP Diliman Department of Philosophy; specialist in classical Greek ethics, Plato, ancient virtue theory, and moral psychology.

nodes.name: Lumberto Guce Mendoza
nodes.tradition: Philosophy of Language, Wittgenstein, Social & Political Philosophy, STS, P4C
nodes.dissertation: Naturalized Epistemology and Cognitive Architecture
nodes.bio: Associate Professor specializing in Wittgenstein, Eastern philosophy, Philosophy for Children, logic as Gestalt, Science, Technology and Society (STS), and research ethics.

nodes.name: Peter A. Sy
nodes.tradition: AI Ethics, Bioethics, Social Philosophy, Data Privacy
nodes.dissertation: Informational Privacy and Justice in Technological Society (MA Thesis)
nodes.bio: Associate Professor and pioneer in AI ethics, bioethics, and informational privacy; former University Data Protection Officer and CSSP faculty leader.

nodes.name: Nicolo M. Masakayan
nodes.tradition: Social & Political Philosophy, Ethics, Epistemic Injustice
nodes.dissertation: Democratic Deliberation and Epistemic Injustice in Public Discourse

nodes.name: Joseph Raz

nodes.name: John Randolph Lucas
nodes.tradition: Philosophy of Mathematics, Gödelian Arguments, Metaphysics

nodes.name: Emmanuel Q. Fernando
nodes.tradition: Philosophy of Law, Jurisprudence, Mathematical Logic, Legal Positivism, Ethics
nodes.dissertation: The Role and Logic of Substantive Reasons in Adjudication
nodes.bio: Son of former Chief Justice Enrique M. Fernando; recruited by Armando Bonifacio into the faculty in 1975 as one of the celebrated 'Bonifacio Boys'. Earned his MA at UPD on Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems, studied mathematical logic at Cambridge (Gonville & Caius), and completed his DPhil at Oxford (Merton College) under Joseph Raz and J.R. Lucas. Full Professor of Philosophy, Law, and Physics for over 40 years; Department Chair from 2004–2005. The annual Emmanuel Q. Fernando Philosophy Undergraduate Conference is celebrated in his honor by the UP Diliman Department of Philosophy.

historical_eras.title: Department of Philosophy and Psychology
historical_eras.description: Established in 1910 within the College of Liberal Arts under Dr. Henry S. Townsend. Served as the colonial-era nursery for early Filipino civil servants and intellectuals.

historical_eras.title: Post-War Exodus & Rebirth at Palma Hall
historical_eras.description: Following the devastating Battle of Manila and destruction of Padre Faura facilities, the University moved to Diliman, Quezon City. Dr. Ricardo R. Pascual founded the independent Department of Philosophy, embedding analytic philosophy.

historical_eras.title: Independent Department of Philosophy
historical_eras.description: The premier center of analytic philosophy in the Philippines, expanding into bioethics, philosophy for children, logic, and contemporary socio-political critique.
